uzo.purpose: Offers actions for one object behind a single button: edit, duplicate, delete.

instead.kialo: A menu that leads to pages is a navigation, because an action menu fires actions on one object and a navigation moves a person through the application (G6: Menü alone is the navigado's word).
A menu whose entries are values of one field is a select, because the choice stays as the field's value and is sent with the form; a menu entry fires once and holds nothing.
A menu with one entry hides an action behind a click, because a person opens it only to find one command; one action is a button with its name.

boundary.kialo: A menu that opens a second menu beside an entry needs a pointer path and a second focus path; Fundamento does not support it — group the entries with a separator or split them over two menus.

An entry that stays checked is a setting, not an action, because it holds a state after the menu closed; a person decides whether it is a switch beside the object or a menu of checkable items (role menuitemcheckbox) in a later step.

containers.name: record-header
containers.kialo: The actions on one record stand in its head, because the head names the object the actions act on.

with.kialo: The actions on one row of a table are a menu behind one button in the row, because a button per action would fill the row with controls; the tabelo sends its row actions here.
The trigger of a menu is a button, because a menu opens on a command; with an icon alone it carries the name of the menu as its label (icon-meaning-named).
An entry may carry an icon before its word, because the sign is read faster than the word — and never alone, the word names the action.
Groups of entries are separated by a line, because a line says that the entries above and below belong to different things (edit and duplicate; delete).
